item.title: Please join me in the 30x30 Challenge!
item.description:
Dear Partners:

In August 2020, the City of Columbus announced the 30x30 Challenge to ensure that every aspect of workforce and supplier diversity is inclusive and representative of the demographics that make up Ohio’s capital city. I kindly ask that you consider being among the first to join me on this journey.

As the leader of an organization with over 9,000 employees, I am committed to leading by example and taking action to expand the City’s workforce diversity. We started by taking a look in the mirror and measuring ourselves against the 30x30 goals, the details of which can be found below. Over the past year, the City’s Office of Diversity and Inclusion has been diligently performing this work from within, raising the bar for the City of Columbus and those we serve in the community.

Below you will find details on this important new initiative. My team will follow up within the next few weeks to share additional information.

What is the 30x30 Challenge?

The 30x30 Challenge is another tool for the City of Columbus to measure and eliminate racial disparities in the workforce, including how race and other factors contribute to disparities in job opportunities and equitable pay for women. This effort seeks to transform workplace cultures and establish a precedent for the City and all Columbus employers by encouraging them to strive for the following growth by the end of 2023:

  • 30% workforce diversity representation
  • 30% growth in supplier diversity spend
  • 30% executive leadership
  • 30% board and commission representation

How it works

You will receive an email from the Office of Diversity and Inclusion with detailed instructions and a link to the 30x30 Challenge website. From there, you will enter your baseline information according to your industry. This is a self-monitored and self-managed exercise. We ask that you update your information every quarter. Everyone who participates will be able to view industry-specific information on the website. We will ultimately share the overall results and assess our collective impact.

Your role

  • Provide your organization’s contact information and logo.
  • Provide your organization’s baseline metrics:
    • Workforce data (e.g., race/ethnicity, gender, age range, Veteran status, LGBTQ+, disability, tenure, etc.)
    • Supplier diversity spend (e.g., MBE, WBE, LGBTQ+, veteran, disability, industry, etc.)
    • Executive leadership
    • Boards and commissions representation
  • Update your metrics on a quarterly basis.
  • Create or continue to create strategies, programming and policies to assist in reaching or exceeding the designated goals.
  • There may be a time when we ask you to publicly share some of your best practices. (This would be voluntary, not mandatory.)

The city’s role

  • Provide support, resources and tools to assist all participating businesses and organizations.
  • Maintain open communication on a consistent basis.
  • Update the 30x30 Challenge website with new information.

I know that many of you have already implemented changes to address systemic racism in the workplace, and I applaud your efforts. I truly believe in our collective potential to effect change and build a more dynamic, inclusive and equitable Columbus.

Thank you,
